notes: Identity verified from the supplied text: title Getting a Job: Is There a Motherhood Penalty?; Shelley J. Correll, Stephen Benard, and In Paik; copyright 2007; AJS Volume 112 Number 5 (March 2007): 1297–1338. The full article text includes laboratory methods, results, tables, audit study, conclusions and references. Its printed ending page is 1338, whereas the neutral reference says 1339. DOI is not printed in the supplied text, so DOI identity is not independently established; title/authors/journal/year identify the referenced primary report. No PDF path supplied. The p.26 locator identifies Table 4. Printed coefficient retained on its binary-logistic scale, without exponentiation or standardization. N is explicitly printed for the critical model, not inferred from df or summed. The supplied description explicitly names female participants; interpreted as the Female participant evaluator-gender predictor in the Hire? model. It is not the Female applicant predictor (1.21). The phrase versus other applicants in the description conflates evaluator and applicant roles: this coefficient compares female versus male evaluators' hiring recommendations, controlling applicant characteristics. No applicant-sex contrast is substituted. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Canonical significance legends use the extraction glyph ! for less-than. Conservative final disposition: target correspondence remains ambiguous because the supplied description combines female participants and a comparison with other applicants. Candidate Hire? coefficients are Female participant .606 (SE .199, *** P < .001) versus Female applicant 1.21 (SE .365, *** P < .001). Neither candidate is selected. The common model N=188 participants is retained only as a candidate, not a positive field. Target_match is null and all field confidences are false.
